doc.title: Glenn Zottola interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 7, 2020

title: First paying gig with Teagarden and Hackett at eleven
summary: Never worried about making a living; early TV work with Chubby Jackson led to a gig at eleven with Bobby Hackett and Jack Teagarden.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: So let me ask you if there was — you know you were surrounded by music, your parents had a jazz club, was there ever a question in your head about how you were going to make a living?

Never. Well since my whole family was musicians, the phone kind of started ringing after television. You know I didn’t have to go out and hustle up gigs. So I was fortunate in that way. No I never had any thought of that, I just followed my heart you know.
Do you remember the first paying gig you ever had and how much you made?
Yeah. I was doing the Chubby — you know Chubby Jackson, right?

So I did a lot of performances on the “Little Rascals Show.” Okay? And you know they had a big band on that show with Don Lamond was on drums, they had a fantastic band. So Chubby hooked me up with his son, Duffy, and we started a little group together with Duffy. And then he got me a gig, my first big gig at eleven years old guesting with Bobby Hackett and Jack Teagarden. So I think that was my first big gig.
And what did you make? © Fillius Jazz Archive -4-
I don’t know. But we went to a diner afterwards and hung out with Jack and Bobby, you know.
Yes you can’t buy that and you can’t separate it from the music, that fraternity and those like being around those guys.
